title: Negotiating Risk Boundaries in AI for Policing Through Mixed-Stakeholder Deliberation
abstract: arXiv:2608.05418v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: AI tools are being increasingly adopted in policing in the UK and worldwide. Racial bias is a known and well-documented risk, yet representatives of affected communities are rarely included in decisions about AI adoption. We present results from a mixed-stakeholder deliberation workshop bringing together 30 community representatives, police officers, and academics to assess the risks of 13 AI use cases in policing, with an explicit focus on racial bias. We found that participants were broadly open to AI adoption, rejecting only three use cases outright -- most notably recidivism risk assessment, where objections targeted the premise rather than the implementation. Our analysis reveals that foregrounding racial equity did not narrow the deliberation. translated_title: 通过多方利益相关者协商探讨警务人工智能的风险边界
translated_abstract: 人工智能工具在英国及世界各地的警务工作中正得到越来越多的应用。种族偏见是一种已知且有充分记录的风险，然而受影响社区的代表却很少被纳入关于人工智能应用的决策之中。我们展示了一次汇聚30名社区代表、警察和学者的混合利益相关者协商研讨会的成果，该研讨会评估了警务工作中13个人工智能应用场景的风险，并明确聚焦于种族偏见问题。我们发现，参与者对人工智能的应用总体持开放态度，仅有三个应用场景被完全拒绝——其中最值得关注的是再犯风险评估，反对意见针对的是其前提假设而非具体实施方式。我们的分析表明，突出种族公平性并未使讨论范围收窄。相反，讨论逐渐聚焦于一系列根本性问题：这个工具是否真正有效？它是否能带来切实的益处？这些益处是否能惠及所有人？
tldr: 该研究通过汇聚社区代表、警察和学者的协商研讨会发现，各方对警务人工智能应用总体持开放态度，且讨论并未局限于种族偏见，而是聚焦于工具是否真正有效、能否带来切实收益以及收益能否惠及所有人这些根本性问题。
en_tdlr: A mixed-stakeholder deliberation workshop involving community representatives, police officers, and academics found broad openness to AI adoption in policing, with discussions centering not on racial bias but on fundamental questions of whether the tools actually work, deliver genuine benefits, and benefit everyone.
